extraction.agency_name: Blind Industries and Services of Maryland
extraction.parent_department: Blind Industries and Services of Maryland

findings.title: Until September 2015, BISM Had Not Formally Adopted Strategies to Accomplish Organizational Goals It Established in 2013
findings.description: BISM had not formally adopted strategies to accomplish organizational goals established in 2013 and has not developed action plans or measures to assess success. Action plans are essential for achieving goals such as increasing sales to $250 million and employment to 750 individuals.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that BISM a. develop action plans for its strategic initiatives identifying steps to be taken, those individuals responsible for completing the tasks and related timeframes; b. develop performance measures to assess whether the actions taken are achieving desired results; and c. conduct ongoing monitoring of plans and outcomes.

findings.title: BISM Conducts Outreach Programs to Inform Maryland Residents of Available Services and the Needs of Blind Individuals Requesting Services Appear to be Met
findings.description: BISM conducts outreach programs using various communication methods. Representatives from State and county agencies indicated they were unaware of any individuals who requested services BISM offers that had not been served.

findings.title: BISM Has Assumed More Financial Responsibility Over Its Various Rehabilitation and Training Programs Offered to Blind Individuals
findings.description: The Maryland General Assembly expressed intent for BISM to move toward self-sufficiency. Annual State grant awards declined from $1.9 million in 1998 to approximately $531,000 in fiscal years 2012-2015. In fiscal year 2015, total rehabilitation and training expenditures were $1,579,533.

dollar_amounts.context: total rehabilitation and training expenditures for fiscal year 2015

findings.title: Many Former BISM Students Completing the CORE Program Have Reported Achieving Successful Post-Training Outcomes, but BISM Has Not Established a Process for Tracking Student Satisfaction with Some of Its Services
findings.description: Many former students reported successful outcomes such as employment or college enrollment. However, BISM does not survey participants of in-home training, workshops, or one-day programs to assess performance and client satisfaction.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that BISM establish a formal process for determining and tracking student/client satisfaction for all its training and rehabilitation services.

findings.title: Pricing Committees Established by State Law Had Not Conducted a Comprehensive Review of the Prices of BISM’s Supplies and Services Available For Sale to State Agencies
findings.description: The independent pricing committees have not performed a comprehensive price review of all supplies and services. Consequently, there is no assurance that prices reflect fair market prices as required by law.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that a. the Pricing and Selection Committee set the fair market prices of all BISM products and services for sale to the State; b. the Committee maintain a current list of those products and services... c. DGS make the Committee approved list... available to State agencies; and d. BISM retain documentation...

findings.title: Based on Our Review of Selected BISM Products, BISM Prices, On an Overall Basis, Were Competitive with the Prices of Similar Third-Party Competitor Products Offer For Sale to The Public
findings.description: BISM prices were competitive with Internet prices for similar third-party products. Limitations included shipping costs, product quality variance, and volume pricing discounts.

findings.title: Differing Legal Opinions and a Court Ruling Raise Questions as to Whether Products BISM Sells to State Agencies Must Meet the Direct Blind Labor Hours Threshold Specified in State Law
findings.description: Legal counsel reaffirmed that only products with at least 75 percent blind labor qualify for procurement preference. BISM disagrees based on a 1995 court ruling, and does not maintain records of direct blind labor hours.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that BISM take necessary action to ensure compliance with State law.

findings.title: The Annual Evaluation of the Chief Executive Officer Was Not Directly Linked to Specific Measurable Goals and the CEO Performance Bonus Program Was Not Defined and Documented
findings.description: The annual evaluation was not directly linked to specific measurable goals. The CEO's performance bonus program was not defined, though it accounted for 52 percent of compensation.

dollar_amounts.context: CEO's fiscal year 2016 Board approved compensation
